Summary (full text)

Camera wyze-t20x-jxf23 (T20) in the light box with the SpyderCheckr 24 chart, lamps 3000 K. Both stacks ran on the same camera, the same chart position and the same light: the open stack (open-tx-isp + OpenIMP + timps) and the vendor stack (Ingenic ISP module + vendor libimp + timps built for it), one after the other.

Result: 57 pass, 2 fail (1 invalid by test setup, 1 issue), 108 info/warn, 1 flaky (failed 1 of 3, repeated), 1 planned checks not run in these runs.

Failed checks: chart grey BG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral) (open 0.9012, vendor 0.9219; pass = open as close to 1.0 as the vendor or closer (+0.02)); OSD text item appears (open changed 1.8 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % , vendor changed 1.4 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % ; pass = > 2 % of the item box changes by > 40 and > 5 x the no-text A/A pair; box 764,482-988,566; pass = > 2 % of the item box changes by > 40 and > 5 x the no-text A/A pair; box 764,482-988,566; open repeated: 2/2 failed (values changed 1.8 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % | changed 1.6 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 %); vendor repeated: 2/2 failed (values changed 1.4 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 % | changed 1.4 % of the item box / A/A 0.0 %)).

Passed: frame luma p1_day (AE target, default comp 128); frame luma p1_night (AE target, default comp 128); chart grey RG (AWB, unclipped grey patches, 1.0 = neutral); p1_day dE00 mean, unclipped patches; p1_day dE00 mean, grey-normalised; grey row tone slope; MTF50 median of 8 chart edges (cycles/pixel); 10-90 % edge rise median (px); H.264 FixQP 25: decodes clean; H.264 FixQP 25: blocking / ghosting flags; ...

How to read: "pass" means the open stack is equal to or better than the vendor stack within the tolerance named in each row; matched-exposure rows (A2) compare the same integration time and gain on both stacks, read back from the ISP.

A5 Encoder (H.264): open vs vendor, same settings

Cells = open / vendor. Static chart scene, lamps on, day pinned, streamer restarted per case with a /tmp conf. Bytes per frame and P/I from ffprobe -show_frames (frames before the first IDR and, for CBR, the first seconds are ignored). PSNR / SSIM (luma) of every decoded frame (SSIM every 2th) against the mean image of the stack's own H.264 FixQP reference recording, so the ISP difference between the stacks drops out; sensor noise stays in (see the noise-floor row): an encoder that smooths noise can score higher than the reference. blk = blockiness of the error image (step across 8-px borders / step inside, 1.00 = no block structure); GOP drift = PSNR of the IDR minus the last P of the GOP. n/a = the streamer of that stack did not take the setting.

anomalies: Night IR snapshots report layout BAD-uv-static (uv_static 7/7): U and V are 0.000 and every per-frame UV value is exactly 128.00/128.00. This is expected for a monochrome night mode, but it is classified BAD by the snap checker, so either the checker or the pipeline needs review., The d1d4 vision check reports the picture nearly black with no IR illumination and colour noise, so IR night mode was apparently not active. This contradicts the ISP mode=Night readout and suggests an IR-cut/IR LED control problem or a daynight state mismatch., Excessive repeated firmware activity: T20FW switch_wdr/mesh_reload runs many times back-to-back within about 5 ms (4 times at 3813 s, 8 times at 3835 s, and the same pattern in reload 9) with an identical mode=0 and identical tables. This points to redundant WDR/mesh reload loops in the driver., After LAMPS_OFF the pin_day AE exposure jumped to 61960.8 (from 3475 under lamps), and in the lamps-off aeresp test Y fell from 103.6 to 12.2. That means the scene is underexposed in the dark while pinned to day; this is likely expected, but AE took 18.33 s (275 frames) to settle., The lamps-on AE overshoot is 21.3% (130% peak deviation). This is informational, not a failure.; severity: medium

run-t20-1109-1515comparebothinfoSharpness and noise are a wash. The vendor stack pushes exposure and saturation, which looks punchier but clips highlights: the light-yellow patch and the top greys turn white. The open-source stack preserves highlights and tonal separation, giving more accurate light colours, at the cost of a slight warm cast and somewhat less saturation. For accuracy, Picture 1 is better; for eye-candy, Picture 2 is.
better_overall: Picture 1 (open-source stack), narrowly; open_better: Highlight handling: the yellow-green patch (row 2, col 4) keeps its pale yellow tint and the top-row light greys stay separated, while the vendor image clips both to near-white, Tonal gradation: the grey ramp steps are more evenly spaced and the brightest patches are not blown, Colour accuracy on light/pastel patches: the pink, salmon and light-yellow patches stay closer to their true hue instead of washing out, Sharpness and noise: essentially equal to the vendor image, with clean patch edges and similar fine noise; vendor_better: Slightly more saturated, punchier primaries: the yellow, yellow-green, orange and blue patches look more vivid, Marginally brighter overall exposure and higher midtone contrast, which gives a crisper first impression, White balance: the background and white patches are a touch more neutral, whereas the open-source image has a faint warm/yellow cast in the light greys
run-t20-1109-1515triagebothinfoOne likely real defect on the open stack: intermittent decode errors in the CBR test after restart. The OSD failure on both stacks points to a test-criterion problem. The vendor h264 reference failures after restart look like a harness or capture issue. The vendor WB settle failure is unclear; check the light-box illuminant.
open cbr measured bitrate: real (Two decode errors in the stream fail the check outright, regardless of bitrate. Intermittent (1 of 3 attempts) after restart, which suggests a real encoder or restart stability defect worth reproducing.) | open OSD text item appears: invalid (The vendor stack also fails, with a similar 1.4 % change. That points to the method: the 2 % threshold or the item box is likely too strict or misplaced for size-48 text, rather than a defect in the open stack.) | vendor time to a stable picture: WB preset 1 at 3000 K: unclear (Vendor reference only. Not stable within 60 s could be slow vendor AWB, or light-box flicker or a mismatch with the 3000 K source; check the illuminant.) | vendor h264 ref_qp10: invalid (No decodable frames after restart, and ref_end fails the same way. Most likely a capture or restart-timing problem in the test, not an encoder output issue; vendor reference anyway.) | vendor h264 ref_end: invalid (Same no-decodable-frames-after-restart pattern as ref_qp10, which points to stream capture or restart handling in the harness.) | vendor OSD text item appears: invalid (Both stacks fail with a 0 % A/A difference and only a small changed area. The pass criterion or box geometry likely does not fit the rendered text.)

Method

  • Same camera, same chart position, same lamps; open stack first, then the vendor ISP module + vendor libimp are loaded from /tmp (nothing flashed); the camera returns to the flashed image at the end (module reload or reboot).
  • P1 = camera defaults (AE, AWB, comp 128). P2 = matched exposure: the same integration time and gains on both stacks, set inside the streamer and read back from the ISP; rows whose read-back differs are marked verify=FAIL and not compared.
  • A/A: point p2_a is measured twice (p2_a, p2_a2); the relative difference is the repeatability of the method. A difference between the stacks counts only beyond 2 x that spread (floor 5 %).
  • NV12 noise is measured on raw NV12 frames from the streamer (no JPEG in the path): temporal standard deviation per pixel over the burst, mean over Y 32..224, and U/V.
  • Colour: SpyderCheckr 24 detected automatically, sRGB -> Lab (D50), CIEDE2000 against the Datacolor default values (D50 assumed, not batch specific); 'grey-normalised' removes the white-balance cast first.
  • Sharpness: slanted-edge method on the chart's outer patch edges, frames averaged against noise; JPEG snapshot path.
  • SSIM/PSNR (when run): both stacks record the same static chart scene at the same bitrate; each stream is decoded and compared against a high-bitrate capture of the SAME stack (reference), so the number is the encoder loss of that stack; a cross-stack comparison on static frames is listed separately and includes the ISP difference.
  • Encoder (A5): both stacks get the same timps settings (codec, rc_mode, qp / bitrate, gop) through a /tmp conf and a streamer restart; the recordings come over RTSP (ffmpeg -c copy). The reference is a mean image, because single NV12 frames are not frame-aligned with the stream; the scene is static, so every decoded frame can be compared with it. A second reference at the end of the phase shows whether the scene or the AE moved in between.
  • Lamp switches are made by a person on a marker (NEED_* file); the times above are the marker times.
